slides.title: Assessment 1. Module: Organization of laboratory services. Medical ethics and deontology
bullets: Organization of laboratory services. Medical ethics and deontology
Assessment — 6 h

slides.title: Lesson outline
bullets: Textbook material: Module 1 review: organising the laboratory and safety; Module 1 review: quality control
Reference values: Reference values and decision limits
Practice: Q&A: 6 + 3

slides.title: Module 1 review: organising the laboratory and safety
bullets: The laboratory occupies spacious, bright rooms; samples are prepared in a separate room; benches resist chemicals; work with harmful vapours is done in a fume hood.

Responsibility is shared: the head answers for quality, equipment, reagents and reporting; the laboratory physician performs tests and internal/external control; the technician prepares material, draws blood and keeps records.
All samples are potentially infectious: gloves, no mouth pipetting, single-use scarifiers, hepatitis B vaccination.

slides.title: Module 1 review: organising the laboratory and safety
bullets: Acid or alkali exposure — rinse with plenty of water without neutralising; a cut with infected material — wash with soap under running water and disinfect with 70% alcohol or iodine.
Hazardous reagents are kept on lower shelves and labelled; electrical instruments are earthed.
Automation goes in two directions: processes inside the laboratory and the link to the hospital information system.

slides.title: Module 1 review: quality control
bullets: Internal quality control is done daily, in every analytical series, and covers three phases: pre-analytical, analytical and final.
Its basis is a standardised control material and a control chart; the material comes from approved factory products or from leftover samples.
Control material is handled as carefully as infectious material; the data sheet is read.
Sources of analytical error: general laboratory factors, reagents, control material, samples and the instrument.

slides.title: Module 1 review: quality control
bullets: Pre-analytical factors: registration errors, biological and iatrogenic factors, collection conditions; blood is drawn in the morning, fasting, lying or sitting.
In the final phase the result is checked against the referral, compared with previous results and the dispatch time is shown.

slides.title: Reference values and decision limits
rows: x̄ and SD from at least 20 measurements on different days measurement

slides.title: Types of systematic errors:
Control material prepared from horse serum can be used in the following cases:
options: turbidity less than 0.2 units. Extinction (cuvette 0.3 cm; wavelength 630–690 nm)

slides.title: Not used in quality control of coagulation tests:
options: Fresh pooled plasma from many donors (at least 20 people), standard lyophilized human plasma for calibration
plasma prepared from human plasma with a precise concentration of coagulation factors (normal and pathological)
control plasma deficient in some coagulation factors
Fresh plasma obtained from a donor

slides.title: Quality management method that does not require control materials:
options: Study of parallel samples, repeat testing of the sample

slides.title: Interlaboratory quality control makes it possible to:
options: Compare the quality of work of several laboratories
Assess the quality of the methods used

slides.title: It is proposed to use the following for quality control of biochemical tests:
options: ready-made commercially produced serum (liquid or lyophilized)

slides.title: Safety rules in laboratories (occupational safety and fire safety)?
bullets: 1. Laboratory safety system: a written safety plan and SOPs, a responsible person, regular staff training (at hiring and periodically), an emergency plan and drills.

2. Electrical safety: mark, take out of service and repair a damaged socket/equipment; connecting/disconnecting equipment to the mains with wet hands is prohibited; mains near water must be grounded; during repair, disconnect from power and use "lockout/tagout".

slides.title: Safety rules in laboratories (occupational safety and fire safety)?
bullets: 3. Sources of fire hazard: flammable solvents, open flame, gas cylinders. Prevention: only the minimum amount at the workplace, store solvents in a special fire-resistant cabinet, do not leave open flame unattended, keep flammables away from fire, keep aisles and emergency equipment accessible.

4. Action in case of fire (RACE): rescue people, raise the alarm, close doors to confine the fire, evacuate/extinguish. Using a fire extinguisher (PASS): pull the pin, aim at the base of the fire, squeeze the lever, sweep side to side.

slides.title: Safety rules in laboratories (occupational safety and fire safety)?
bullets: 5. Choose the extinguisher type to match the fire class (A – solid combustibles, B – flammable liquids/gases, C – energized equipment – with a non-conductive agent); if clothing catches fire – "stop, drop and roll", a fire blanket or emergency shower (if there is no chemical/current).

6. Every employee must know the location of emergency equipment: fire extinguisher, alarm, exit routes, emergency shower/eyewash, first aid kit; do not work alone, wear suitable PPE (lab coat, goggles, gloves).

slides.title: Safety rules when working with biological material (biosafety)?
bullets: 1. Biological safety consists of measures to protect the worker, the community and the environment from infectious agents and patient specimens; the basis is a risk assessment for each task (collect information → assess risk → control strategy → implement measures → review).

2. Biosafety levels (BSL-1…4): BSL-1 – agents not known to cause disease in healthy adults; BSL-2 – agents causing disease of varying severity (HBV, HIV, Salmonella, etc.); work with blood, body fluids and tissues is usually carried out under BSL-2 conditions; BSL-3/4 – severe/dangerous airborne agents.

slides.title: Safety rules when working with biological material (biosafety)?
bullets: 3. Standard microbiological practice: eating, drinking, smoking, cosmetics and food storage are prohibited in the laboratory; mouth pipetting is prohibited – use mechanical pipetting devices; wash hands after work and when leaving; long hair must be tied back.

4. Personal protective equipment: lab coat, gloves (not worn outside the laboratory, changed when contaminated, disposable gloves are not washed or reused), eye/face protection when there is a splash risk; remove PPE without self-contamination.

slides.title: Safety rules when working with biological material (biosafety)?
bullets: 5. Sharps: do not recap needles by hand, do not bend/break them; place used needles and syringes immediately into a puncture-proof container; pick up broken glass not with hands but with a brush/forceps.

6. Reducing aerosols and splashes: aerosol-generating work (centrifuging, mixing, opening) in a biological safety cabinet or in sealed centrifuge cups; for spills, decontaminate according to an established procedure.

slides.title: Safety rules when working with biological material (biosafety)?
bullets: 7. Decontamination and waste: disinfect work surfaces at the end of work and after every spill; decontaminate cultures and infectious material before disposal (preferably by autoclave), transport in a sealed container with a biohazard sign.

8. Staff health: occupational health requirements (including vaccination); after a needlestick or mucosal contamination – wash immediately, inform the supervisor and follow the post-exposure prophylaxis procedure; those working with blood follow the "bloodborne pathogens" rules.

slides.title: Medical ethics and deontology?
bullets: 1. Medical ethics are the moral principles governing a health worker's attitude toward the patient, colleagues and society; deontology is the study of professional duty and rules of conduct.
2. Core principles: putting the patient's interest first, non-maleficence, patient autonomy and voluntary informed consent, non-discrimination (diagnosis and services only according to medical need).

slides.title: Medical ethics and deontology?
bullets: 3. Confidentiality: test results and the patient's personal data are medical confidentiality – disclosed only to authorized persons; this obligation continues after the patient's death. In the laboratory: do not give a result to a stranger by telephone, do not leave forms in view, restrict access to the electronic system.

4. Professional competence and accountability: continuous learning, professional development; honesty – record and correct errors without concealing them (it is forbidden to "fix" a result); report critical results to the physician immediately.

slides.title: Medical ethics and deontology?
bullets: 5. Relations with colleagues: respect and cooperation, clear communication between the laboratory technician, physician and nurse; do not criticize a colleague in front of the patient.
6. In Uzbekistan the code of ethics and deontology of medical workers was approved by MoH Order No. 88 of 24 March 2022 – know its main requirements (check the text on lex.uz).
